content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: approve P0 (no intraday change).","why":"Both queues are short because of a sick wave. Payments logged 15 absences against a usual 2.8, and general logged 13 against a usual 2.6, mostly agents who went home unwell after lunch. At 15:15 payments had 30 of 42 planned agents on the phones with service level at 49%, and general had 29 of 40 at 61.6%. Call volume is close to forecast, so this is a staffing problem, not a demand one. The disruption window is shown as 20:00-20:00, which means the model sees no remaining gap to cover. For that window it predicts 100% service level on both queues against the 80% target, with 0% abandons and no extra cost or policy issues. P0 was the only option evaluated, so there are no alternatives to compare on cost, customer impact or risk to the other queue.","trade_offs":["Costs nothing (INR 0) and breaks no policy.","The predicted 100% applies to a zero-length window, so it says little about the shortfall still visible at 15:15. If the gap is still open, it is not covered by this plan.","No alternative plans were generated, so the cost or benefit of acting now is unknown."],"watch":"Check that payments (49% at 15:15) and general (61.6%) are actually recovering. If agent counts stay well below plan or service level stays under 80%, ask for the plan to be rerun with staffing options, and bring in the duty manager if the gap persists."}
